entries.probe: tests/test_nightqc.py::test_a_LEADING_COMMENT_does_not_hide_the_header — every variant reads a window that still extends to EOF, so the file's LAST line is present in all of them: seeking to 2 or 0 instead of the end makes `size` small and `max(0, size-8192)` clamps to 0, i.e. the whole file; a wider window (`2<<13`, `1<<14`) reads more; `max(1, …)` shifts the start by one byte and `seek(1, SEEK_END)` by one the other way, neither of which can remove the final newline-delimited row. They change how much I/O the O(1) promise does, never which stamp is returned — a cost property, and one no value assertion can observe.
